declarations.description:
A Fire chart drawn from data given as a property: line, area, bar and stacked charts, quadrants, sparklines, donuts and
progress rings, heat grids and strips. The element is the chart's root: it carries the root class of its type
(`fd-chart` for the cartesian types and the quadrant, `fd-sparkline`, `fd-donut` or `fd-heatgrid`) and the markup form's data-* attributes, holds the data
as the markup form's `<script type="application/json">`, and Fire's charts module draws the chart inside it, so it
looks and behaves exactly like the markup form. Setting `data` (or any attribute) redraws it, without the entrance
animation. Changing `type` to another kind of chart (say from `line` to `donut`) is not supported: render a new
element (in React or Vue, give it a new `key`).

Attributes mirror the markup form's `data-*` attributes; each applies to the types named. A function in the data
(a custom `yFormat`) is kept for cartesian charts, which are drawn from the object itself; the other types are
drawn from the JSON, so their formats are names.
declarations.name: FdChart

members.name: type
members.description: Chart type: `line` (default), `area`, `bar`, `stacked`, `quadrant`, `sparkline`, `donut` or `heatgrid` (the markup form's `data-fd-chart`, or its class for the other three).

members.name: variant
members.description: Variant of a type: `bars` for a sparkline (`data-type="bars"`), `progress` for a donut (a progress ring, `data-type="progress"`), `strip` for a heat grid (`data-variant="strip"`).

members.name: data
members.description: The chart's data: a `ChartConfig` for the cartesian types, a `QuadrantConfig` for a quadrant, an array of numbers for a sparkline, a `DonutConfig`, a `HeatgridConfig` or (strip) a `StripConfig`. As an attribute, JSON.

members.name: height
members.description: Height in px. Cartesian: the plot, 80 to 900 (default 240). Quadrant: the plot, 160 to 900 (default 360). Sparkline: the drawing (default from CSS, 24).

members.name: width
members.description: Sparkline: width in px (default from CSS, 80).

members.name: legend
members.description: Cartesian: show the built-in legend, whose items toggle series.

members.name: grid
members.description: Cartesian: grid lines, `dashed` (default), `solid` or `none`.

members.name: hideLabels
members.description: Quadrant: hide the names beside the points (`data-labels="none"`).

members.name: state
members.description: Cartesian and quadrant: `loading` (a skeleton; needs no data) or `empty` (the empty state).

members.name: label
members.description: Accessible name override (all types); a progress ring also shows it as its caption.

members.name: yFormat
members.description: Cartesian: value format when the data gives none, `number`, `compact`, `percent`, `ms` or `credits`.

members.name: values
members.description: Sparkline: values as text, `3,5,4,8`, when `data` is not set.

members.name: area
members.description: Sparkline: fill the area under the line.

members.name: dot
members.description: Sparkline: mark the last point.

members.name: invert
members.description: Sparkline: lower is better, so a falling trend is coloured as good.

members.name: fluid
members.description: Sparkline: take the width of its container and redraw when it changes.

members.name: tone
members.description: Sparkline and progress ring: a fixed tone instead of the trend colour or the accent.

members.name: size
members.description: Donut: diameter in px (default 144, progress 96). Heat grid: cell size, `sm`, `md` (default) or `lg`.

members.name: thickness
members.description: Donut: ring thickness in px.

members.name: value
members.description: Progress ring: the value.

members.name: max
members.description: Progress ring: the maximum (default 100).

members.name: format
members.description: Donut: value format when the data gives none (a name, as in `yFormat`).

members.name: #drawn
members.description: Whether this element has drawn a chart yet.

members.name: #scripted
members.description: Whether the chart reads its data from a JSON script (a sparkline and a progress ring read attributes).

members.name: #addedClass
members.description: The root class this element added itself (a class the page set is never taken away).

members.name: #written
members.description: Root attributes this element wrote, so it removes only those.

members.name: #root
members.description: Make the element its component's root: the class, then the attributes.

events.description: A point was clicked, tapped or chosen with Enter. Cartesian: `{ index, label, values }`; strip: `{ index, label, tone, name, href }`.

declarations.description:
A Fire code block that highlights the text it is given. The element is the block's root: it carries
`class="fd-codeblock"` and the markup form's data-* attributes, renders the block's internals (an optional header
or copy button, then `<pre class="fd-codeblock-body"><code data-lang="…">`), puts `code` in it as text and lets
Fire's code module tokenise it into lines, so it looks and behaves exactly like the markup form. Unlike the markup
form inside a framework, Fire never rewrites text nodes the framework owns: changing `code` (or any attribute)
renders the internals afresh.

Languages: `json`, `bash`, `javascript`, `typescript`, `python` and their aliases (`sh`, `curl`, `js`, `ts`, `py`, …);
any other name shows plain text.
declarations.name: FdCode

members.description: Language for highlighting (the markup form's `data-lang` on `<code>`; `lang` is HTML's own attribute).

members.name: lines
members.description: Show line numbers (`data-lines`).

members.name: highlight
members.description: Lines to highlight, `3,5-7` (`data-highlight`).

members.name: collapse

members.name: wrap
members.description: Soft-wrap long lines (`data-wrap`).

declarations.description:
Base class of Fire's custom elements. The element is its component's root: it adds the root class (never removing
a class the page set, and adding it back after each update if a framework replaced `class`), writes the markup
form's data-* attributes from its properties, renders the internals the markup form would hold, runs Fire's
behaviour modules on itself, and redraws when a property changes.

A subclass gives `rootClass()`, `rootAttributes()`, the internals (`markup()`, optional), the Fire modules that
enhance it (`static fire`), a `structure()` string (when it changes, the internals are rendered afresh and
enhanced again), `prepare()` to fill what the template does not carry, and `refresh()` to redraw in place.
declarations.name: FireElement

declarations.description:
One of Fire's icons (a Lucide subset). The element is the icon's root, as `svg.fd-icon` is for the markup form:
it carries `class="fd-icon"`, `data-icon`, `data-size` and `aria-hidden="true"`, so every `.fd-icon` rule applies
to it, direct-child rules such as `.fd-btn > .fd-icon` included. Inside it, an SVG drawn from Fire's sprite fills
it (fire/base.css). Use it in framework code, where an `<i data-icon>` that replaces itself would break the
framework's reconciliation. The icon is decorative: name the control that holds it.

An unknown name draws nothing and logs a warning, as the markup form does.
declarations.name: FdIcon

members.description: Icon name from Fire's set, for example `search` (the markup form's `data-icon`).

members.description: Size in px: 12, 14, 16 (the default), 20, 24 or 32 (the markup form's `data-size`).

declarations.description:
A Fire generative character field: terrain, waves, orbit, rain, grid, flame, halftone or spark. The element is
the field's root: it carries the markup form's `class="fd-ascii"`, `data-fd-ascii="…"`,
the other `data-*` attributes and `aria-hidden="true"`, and Fire's texture module draws its canvas inside it and owns
its size, colour and animation (12 fps on a shared frame loop, paused off screen, one still frame under reduced
motion). Being the field keeps Fire's layering rule, which puts a field between its container's background and its
content, working as it does for the markup form. Changing a property re-reads the settings and redraws.

The field fills its nearest positioned ancestor, or flows at the field height with `inline`. It is decorative.
declarations.name: FdTexture

members.name: pattern
members.description: The field: `terrain` (default), `waves`, `orbit`, `rain`, `grid`, `flame`, `halftone`, `spark` or a registered name (`data-fd-ascii`).

members.name: tone
members.description: Ink: `neutral` (default), `accent`, `contrast` or `strong` (`data-tone`).

members.name: fade
members.description: Fade out toward an edge: `left`, `right`, `top`, `bottom`, `x`, `y` or `radial` (`data-fade`).

members.name: marks
members.description: Draw `chars` (default) or `dots`, halftone discs (`data-style`).

members.name: ramp
members.description: Character ramp: `default`, `soft`, `dense`, `glyph`, `rain`, or a literal ramp such as ` .:-=+*#` (`data-ramp`).

members.name: cell
members.description: Cell size in px, `7x12` (default) or `8` for square (`data-cell`).

members.name: seed
members.description: Seed, a number or a string; defaults to the pattern name, so a page always looks the same (`data-seed`).

members.name: animated
members.description: `true` or `false`; waves, orbit, rain and flame animate by default (`data-animate`; `animate` is a DOM method).

members.name: speed
members.description: Time multiplier, default 1 (`data-speed`).

members.name: intensity
members.description: Luminance multiplier, default 1 (`data-intensity`).

members.name: interactive
members.description: Characters near the pointer step up the ramp (`data-interactive`).

members.name: origin
members.description: `x,y` in 0..1, the centre for orbit, flame, halftone and spark (`data-origin`).

members.name: side
members.description: Terrain: the side that rises, `right` (default) or `left` (`data-side`).

members.name: variant
members.description: Grid: `flat` (default) or `perspective` (`data-variant`).

members.name: shape
members.description: `blob` clips the field to a soft, noisy disc (`data-shape`).

members.name: inline
members.description: Flow in the page at the field height instead of filling the positioned ancestor (`data-inline`).
